conviction_note: The one material unpriced-looking item is guidance: the Aug-11 2026 EBITDA guide ($8.7-9.1B) assumed a $12.50-13.50/MMBtu fee on the ~9% of 2026 cargos still unsold (sensitivity $180-210M per $1), while TTF/JKM ran $24.6-34 against Henry Hub ~$3 from late September to early November, so a raise is likely; but Q3 itself was pre-released on Oct 7 (465.8 TBtu at $6.79), the Aug raise was sold -7.3%, the stock has de-rated ~18% since Oct 26 on Iran-deal hopes that the market reads through to 2027 (sensitivity $650-700M per $1), and the option skew already pays upside. So the findings sum to +2.6 and the scaled number is only +1.1 (p_up 56 x abs 9.5); the gap is the reaction-function discount: the guide raise is a 2026 one-off the market may look through to 2027.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS $0.50 (whisper $0.53) and revenue ~$4.64B, single source (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 2026-11-03: https://finviz.com/news/414164/venture-globals-q3-test-can-record-ebitda-hold-through-summer-after-three-guidance-raises); that preview frames Q3 adjusted EBITDA 'near $2.5B' as validating the guide, but no sourced EBITDA consensus was found, so the reported-quarter finding is capped small. The guidance bar is the company's own: FY2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA $8.7-9.1B, with a $12.50-13.50/MMBtu fee assumed on unsold cargos (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002007855/000200785526000063/vgincq22026earningsrelease.htm, 2026-08-11). The Street's FY26 number is unsourced and may already sit above the guide: Reuters reported Q2 EBITDA missed estimates.

findings.finding: The FY2026 EBITDA guide ($8.7-9.1B, set 2026-08-11) assumes a $12.50-13.50/MMBtu fixed liquefaction fee on the ~9% of 2026 cargos then unsold, at $180-210M of EBITDA per $1. Since then Europe/Asia spot ran far above that: TTF $24.6 / JKM ~$25 on Oct 2, TTF $34.0 / JKM low-$34s on Oct 30, still TTF $28.0 / JKM high-$31s on Nov 6, with Henry Hub ~$2.9-3.1. That is a gross spread of roughly $20-30 against the $13 midpoint. The Q3 fee of $6.79 against $6.45 in Q2 is consistent with open cargos clearing near $18 in Q3. The company should raise or top-end the guide (illustratively, ~120-150 TBtu of Q4 open volume at even $18-20 against $13 is +$0.6-1.0B, i.e. a range toward $9.5B+). It is netted for the Plaquemines Phase 1 COD on Oct 30, which moved Phase 1 output to SPA customers in Q4 (guided) and shrinks the open volume.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide events on confirmed print dates: 2026-03-02 initial 2026 guide +17.44%; 2026-05-12 raise from $5.2-5.8B to $8.2-8.5B (fee assumption $9.50-10.50) +14.2%; 2026-08-11 raise to $8.7-9.1B (fee assumption $12.50-13.50) alongside a reported EBITDA/revenue miss -7.29%. Large raises were bought and a modest raise was sold.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were paying for a 2026 raise, the stock would not have fallen ~18% since Oct 26 into a quarter whose spot spreads were the highest since Dec 2022. The Earnings Whispers preview still frames the bar as 'about $2.4-2.6B a quarter' off the old guide. The market appears to read the Middle East premium as fading and to price 2027 (75% contracted, $650-700M per $1). A Q4 2026 windfall may therefore be treated as a one-off, and that partial pricing is why the size is held below the implied move. The -14 skew (calls bid) shows part of the upside is already paid for.
findings.independence: The price series is independent of the company: Global LNG Hub/JOGMEC weekly updates, https://globallnghub.com/?p=20764 (2026-10-06), https://globallnghub.com/?p=20914 (2026-11-02), https://globallnghub.com/natural-gas-prices-weekly-update-jkm-ttf-and-henry-hub-9-november-2026/ (2026-11-09). The 2026 and 2027 sensitivities and the 91% contracted figure are corroborated in Trefis, https://www.trefis.com/stock/vg/articles/620481/what-is-the-one-risk-every-venture-global-investor-should-know/2026-10-26. Shares the Q3 fee number with the reported-quarter finding only as corroboration (the Oct 7 8-K). The transmission from spot to the guide is inference: the company has not said how much Q4 volume was sold forward before the spike.

findings.finding: Q3 is pre-released by the 2026-10-07 8-K: 465.8 TBtu recognized (Calcasieu Pass 137.7, Plaquemines 328.1; 124 cargos) at an implied weighted fixed liquefaction fee of $6.79/MMBtu, against 466.4 TBtu at $6.45 in Q2, when EBITDA was $2.491B. On Q2's cost base (~$0.52B: 466.4 x 6.45 = $3.01B against $2.49B EBITDA) Q3 implies adjusted EBITDA of ~$2.64B, against the ~$2.5B the preview frames as validating. Revenue maps to roughly $4.7-4.8B against ~$4.64B consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock moved -3.4% on the 2026-10-07 cargo 8-K itself. On 2026-08-11 a reported-quarter miss on revenue and EBITDA (Reuters) accompanied -7.29% despite a guide raise. On 2025-11-10 a revenue beat with an EPS miss saw an initial rise then -1.9% intraday.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the volumes and fee have been public since Oct 7, and any sell-side model already carries them. What remains is a modest gap to a preview bar that may be stale (EW's 'near $2.5B'). If it were fully priced, the preview would cite ~$2.6B+. EPS is noisy because of derivative marks, so the EPS bar of $0.50 is a weak anchor. Capped small because the EBITDA bar is unsourced.
findings.independence: The Q2 comparison is from a different document, the 2026-07-08 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002007855/000200785526000057/vg-20260708.htm), plus the Q2 release. LNG Prime (https://lngprime.com/americas/venture-global-shipped-124-lng-cargoes-in-q3/198047/, 2026-10-08) carries the 124 cargos. Both readings derive from company disclosure.

findings.finding: An arbitral tribunal found Venture Global breached its LNG supply deal with Galp (reported October 2026), with any final award capped at $170M under the seller aggregate cap. It may appear as an accrual or contingency in the Q3 10-Q filed with the release. It sits below operating income and has no path to the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Arbitration headlines have moved the stock: -5.06% when Shell challenged its arbitration defeat in court (itiger, undated in results), and the Nov-2025 sell-off was tied to arbitration and legal disputes. A capped $170M is ~0.6% of market cap.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the ruling was public in October. The only unpriced part is how the 10-Q accrues it and whether management updates the BP damages exposure ($3.7B to >$6B claimed). If the market had fully discounted litigation, the stock would not trade at 32% below its high with debt at ~132% of market value.
findings.independence: The BP claim size and the May 2027 damages hearing are in the Q1 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002007855/000200785526000040/vg-20260331.htm. That is a different document, but the same litigation theme.

outside_window.finding: BP damages hearing on the Calcasieu Pass breach (claim $3.7B to >$6B plus interest), scheduled for May 2027 per the Q1 2026 10-Q.

Per the Q2 call summary, another arbitration hearing begins at the end of November 2026 if no settlement is reached. A settlement announcement could come on the call, but the hearing itself is after the window.

lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the Aug-2026 guide raise was sold -7.3%, so the guidance finding went from +3.0 to +2.5 and p_up from 58 to 56
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): no sourced EBITDA consensus and a single-source revenue bar, so the reported-quarter finding was capped from +0.5 to +0.3 and print_vs_bar cut from 3.0 to 2.0

Lessons 2 and 5 left the Galp one-off at -0.2 (one-off with no path to the guide) and kept the spot-to-guide finding filed despite being transmission inference, because it rests on the company's own published assumption and sensitivity
